## The eddy-diffusion operator on a column (`diffusion_coefficients`) {#sec-ch08-operator}

### Summary

Turbulent mixing in an atmosphere carries each species from where its mixing ratio is high to where it is low.
kintera represents this as a diffusive flux of mixing ratio between neighbouring levels of one column. It uses an
eddy diffusion coefficient given on the faces between levels and zero flux through the bottom and the top. This
scheme builds, for every level, the three coefficients that couple the level to itself and to its two
neighbours. A level's tendency is then a three-term sum.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Tridiagonal coefficients of the flux-form eddy-diffusion tendency, @eq-ch08-operator-tendency.

**Data.** Number densities per level and species; `Kzz`[^rg-5972ec96a93f] and `dzi`[^rg-13c0414b85aa] on the faces.

**Placement.** Called by `diffusion_tendency`, or directly by a caller that builds its own matrix.

**Activation.** Always available; no option.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conserves a weighted column total; uniform mixing ratio gives zero tendency.

**Evidence.** `test_diffusion`; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $y_{j,s}$, number density of species $s$ at level $j$ (any unit, the same for all species);
$n_j = \sum_s y_{j,s}$, total of level $j$; $X_{j,s} = y_{j,s}/n_j$, mixing ratio [-]; $K_{j+1/2}$, eddy diffusion
coefficient on the face between levels $j$ and $j+1$ [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ or $\mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-1}}$];
$h_{j+1/2}$, distance between the centres of levels $j$ and $j+1$ [m or cm]; $N$, the number of levels. These are
proposed for the editor's notation register (none exists for diffusion yet).

The operator has no switch and no default to set. In the code, the `Kzz` is the eddy diffusion coefficient on the
$N-1$ inner faces, the `dzi` is the vector of the $N-1$ face spacings $h_{j+1/2}$, and the `y` argument holds the
number densities, levels first.

### Derivation

The flux of species $s$ through the face $j+1/2$ is the eddy flux of mixing ratio, with the face density taken as
the mean of the two levels:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{j+1/2,s} &= -K_{j+1/2}\, \bar n_{j+1/2}\, \frac{X_{j+1,s} - X_{j,s}}{h_{j+1/2}} \\
\bar n_{j+1/2} &= \tfrac12 \left( n_j + n_{j+1} \right)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch08-operator-flux}

Define the face conductance $D_{j+1/2} = K_{j+1/2}\, \bar n_{j+1/2} / h_{j+1/2}$, so that
$F_{j+1/2,s} = -D_{j+1/2} (X_{j+1,s} - X_{j,s})$. The conductance `D` is computed in `diffusion_coefficients`
({{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_coefficients >}}).

For an inner level $1 \le j \le N-2$, the cell width is the mean of its two face spacings,
$\Delta_j = \tfrac12 (h_{j-1/2} + h_{j+1/2})$, and the finite-volume balance is

$$
\frac{\mathrm d y_{j,s}}{\mathrm d t} = -\frac{F_{j+1/2,s} - F_{j-1/2,s}}{\Delta_j} .
$$

Substituting the fluxes and $X = y/n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d y_{j,s}}{\mathrm d t}
&= \frac{D_{j+1/2} (X_{j+1,s} - X_{j,s}) - D_{j-1/2} (X_{j,s} - X_{j-1,s})}{\Delta_j} \\
&= -\frac{D_{j+1/2} + D_{j-1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_j}\, y_{j,s}
   + \frac{D_{j+1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_{j+1}}\, y_{j+1,s}
   + \frac{D_{j-1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_{j-1}}\, y_{j-1,s} .
\end{aligned}
$$

So the tendency of every level has the form

$$
\frac{\mathrm d y_{j,s}}{\mathrm d t} = A_j\, y_{j,s} + B_j\, y_{j+1,s} + C_j\, y_{j-1,s} ,
$$ {#eq-ch08-operator-tendency}

with, for the inner levels,

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_j &= -\frac{D_{j+1/2} + D_{j-1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_j} \\
B_j &= \frac{D_{j+1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_{j+1}} \\
C_j &= \frac{D_{j-1/2}}{\Delta_j\, n_{j-1}}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch08-operator-inner}

@eq-ch08-operator-inner is computed in `diffusion_coefficients`
({{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_coefficients >}}), on the slices `dz_avg`, `D_lo` and `D_hi`.
The coefficients are the same for every species; only $y_{j,s}$ carries the species index.

At the bottom level the flux through the lower boundary is zero, and the code uses the one face spacing next to
it, $h_{1/2}$, as the width of the level. The top level is treated the same way with $h_{N-3/2}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_0 &= -\frac{D_{1/2}}{h_{1/2}\, n_0} \\
B_0 &= \frac{D_{1/2}}{h_{1/2}\, n_1} \\
C_0 &= 0 \\
A_{N-1} &= -\frac{D_{N-3/2}}{h_{N-3/2}\, n_{N-1}} \\
C_{N-1} &= \frac{D_{N-3/2}}{h_{N-3/2}\, n_{N-2}} \\
B_{N-1} &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch08-operator-boundary}

@eq-ch08-operator-boundary is computed in `diffusion_coefficients`
({{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_coefficients >}}); $C_0$ and $B_{N-1}$ keep the zeros the
coefficient vectors are created with.

Three identities follow; each is exact in exact arithmetic.

::: {#prp-ch08-operator-uniform}
A profile with the same mixing ratio at every level has zero tendency.
:::

If $X_{j,s} = X_s$ for all $j$, every face flux in @eq-ch08-operator-flux is zero, and so is every tendency.

::: {#prp-ch08-operator-level-total}
The operator does not change the total $n_j$ of any level: $\sum_s \mathrm d y_{j,s}/\mathrm d t = 0$.
:::

Summing @eq-ch08-operator-tendency over $s$ gives $A_j n_j + B_j n_{j+1} + C_j n_{j-1}$. For an inner level this is
$\left[-(D_{j+1/2} + D_{j-1/2}) + D_{j+1/2} + D_{j-1/2}\right]/\Delta_j = 0$, and the two boundary rows cancel the
same way.

::: {#prp-ch08-operator-column-total}
With weights $w_0 = h_{1/2}$, $w_j = \Delta_j$ for the inner levels and $w_{N-1} = h_{N-3/2}$, the weighted column
total $\sum_j w_j\, y_{j,s}$ of every species is conserved.
:::

Multiplying each row by its weight gives $w_j\, \mathrm d y_{j,s}/\mathrm d t = -(F_{j+1/2,s} - F_{j-1/2,s})$
with $F_{-1/2,s} = F_{N-1/2,s} = 0$, and the sum over $j$ telescopes to zero. On a uniform grid all weights equal
$h$, so the plain sum of the tendencies over the levels is zero; on a non-uniform grid it is not, because the
boundary levels are weighted with a full face spacing and the inner levels with a mean of two.

No published derivation is cited; the steps above are re-derived from the code at the pin.

### Numerical method

The operator is a three-point, flux-form stencil on cell centres: values $y_{j,s}$ live at level centres,
$K_{j+1/2}$ and $h_{j+1/2}$ on the $N-1$ inner faces, and the boundary faces carry no flux. It is a spatial operator
only. It does not step in time, and it does not iterate. Every coefficient is a whole-tensor expression, so the
same code runs on CPU and CUDA tensors. The order of accuracy on a non-uniform grid is not measured. The stencil
figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| declaration and argument shapes | {{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.hpp diffusion_coefficients >}} | `diffusion_coefficients` | always |
| coefficients | {{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_coefficients >}} | `diffusion_coefficients` | always |
| Python binding | {{< code python/csrc/pydiffusion.cpp bind_diffusion >}} | `bind_diffusion` | always |

: Code map of the eddy-diffusion operator. {#tbl-ch08-operator-code}

1. `n_tot` is the sum of `y` over its last dimension: the level total $n_j$ over every species passed in.
2. `n_avg` is the mean of neighbouring totals, $\bar n_{j+1/2}$, and `D` is `Kzz * n_avg / dzi`.
3. The bottom and top rows are written element by element; the inner rows are written by slices when $N > 2$.
4. The function returns `(A, B, C)`, each of length $N$.

No argument is checked: shapes, signs and zero totals are not validated (see Limits).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_diffusion` | `CoefficientsShape`: length $N$; $C_0 = 0$, $B_{N-1} = 0$ | absolute $10^{-30}$ | `EXPECT_NEAR` in the test |
| `test_diffusion` | `UniformProfileNoFlux`: @prp-ch08-operator-uniform | max below $10^{-10}\, n$ | the test |
| `test_diffusion` | `MassConservation`: @prp-ch08-operator-column-total, uniform grid | relative $10^{-10}$ | the test |

: Tests of the eddy-diffusion operator. {#tbl-ch08-operator-tests}

The cases are in {{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp >}}. They use a uniform grid of 20 levels, two species,
`Kzz` $= 10^5$ and spacing $10^5$ (the test comments say cm and $\mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-1}}$), in float64. They are
instantiated for CPU and CUDA; the CUDA case needs a GPU. @prp-ch08-operator-level-total is not tested directly, and
@prp-ch08-operator-column-total is tested only on a uniform grid. This draft has not run the tests and attaches no run
record (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- One column at a time: `y` must be (levels, species), and `Kzz` and `dzi` are vectors of length $N-1$. A batched call
  is not supported by the slicing; what it does is not tested.
- $N \ge 2$ is needed; with one level the code indexes an empty `D` (read from the code; not tested).
- A level with zero total $n_j$ divides by zero; no guard exists.
- Signs of `Kzz` and `dzi` are not checked.
- The mixing ratio is relative to the sum of all species in `y`. If `y` holds condensed species, they count in
  $n_j$; whether callers pass gases only is not checked here (hypothesis).
:::

The header comment gives `Kzz` in $\mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-1}}$ and `dzi` in cm
({{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.hpp diffusion_tendency >}}). The coefficients depend on them only through
$K/h^2$, so any consistent unit system works, and $A$, $B$, $C$ come out in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The column test of
@sec-ch08-tendency passes SI values.
